[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Cryptographic Basics: Symmetric and Asymmetric Encryption"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Cryptography is the backbone of modern cyber security. It ensures confidentiality, integrity, and non-repudiation of data across networks. At its core, cryptography relies on mathematical algorithms and keys to transform readable plaintext into unreadable ciphertext."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Symmetric Encryption"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Symmetric encryption uses a single, shared secret key for both the encryption of plaintext and the decryption of ciphertext. Because the same key is used by both parties, secure key exchange is the primary challenge in symmetric systems."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"High Performance: Symmetric algorithms are computationally efficient and ideal for encrypting large volumes of data."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Common Algorithms: Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), Data Encryption Standard (DES), and Triple DES (3DES)."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"from cryptography.fernet import Fernet

# Generate a symmetric key
key = Fernet.generate_key()
cipher_suite = Fernet(key)

# Encrypt a message
plain_text = b"Confidential Data"
cipher_text = cipher_suite.encrypt(plain_text)

# Decrypt the message
decrypted_text = cipher_suite.decrypt(cipher_text)"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Asymmetric Encryption"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Asymmetric encryption, also known as public-key cryptography, uses a mathematically linked key pair: a public key for encryption and a private key for decryption. Anyone can use the public key to encrypt a message, but only the holder of the private key can decrypt it."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Solves Key Distribution: Eliminates the need to share a secret key over an insecure channel."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Common Algorithms: RSA (Rivest-Shamir-Adleman), ECC (Elliptic Curve Cryptography), and Diffie-Hellman."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import padding

# Generate private and public keys
private_key = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)
public_key = private_key.public_key()

# Encrypt using public key
message = b"Secure Payload"
ciphertext = public_key.encrypt(
    message,
    padding.OAEP(mgf=padding.MGF1(algorithm=hashes.SHA256()), algorithm=hashes.SHA256(), label=None)
)"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary: Key Differences"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Speed: Symmetric is significantly faster than asymmetric encryption."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scalability: Asymmetric encryption provides better scalability for secure communications across open networks like the internet."},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"In modern cyber security protocols like TLS/SSL, both methods are used in tandem: asymmetric encryption is used to securely exchange a symmetric session key, and symmetric encryption is used for the subsequent data transfer."}]
